findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30 — Any accepted team member can install a team OAuth integration because the team branch checks membership but never requires admin access.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — Credential-sync returns a Fetch `Response`, but this branch reads Axios-style `.data`, so synced Google refreshes throw before updating the token.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The `any` callback and inferred union return erase whether callers receive a Fetch `Response` or an SDK-specific token object, allowing every adapter to assume an incompatible shape without type checking.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — Token validation is coupled to global environment state instead of the response source, so local refreshes that fall back because a credential has no userId are still parsed under the sync-endpoint contract.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:40 — Resolving the app through both the database and `appStoreMetadata` creates two registries that must remain synchronized for the webhook to accept an integration.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42 — The team lookup selects every member userId even though only the team's existence is used, leaving dead query shape and unnecessary coupling to member records.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30 — Any accepted team member can install a team OAuth integration because the team branch checks membership but never requires admin access.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that createOAuthAppCredential.ts was renamed/moved from packages/app-store/_utils/createOAuthAppCredential.ts to packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts. Looking at the diff, only the import paths were changed (lines 6-7 show the import path updates). The actual logic of the function, including the throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam call, was not modified. The finding claims there's a bug where team members without admin access can install integrations, but the diff shows the function still imports and presumably uses throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam. The finding misreads what the diff actually changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The sync request never sends the configured webhook secret/header, so a peer cannot authenticate it without leaving a user-ID token endpoint unauthenticated.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts lines 6-14, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, the code makes a POST request to the sync endpoint but only sends calcomUserId and appSlug in the body. It does not include the CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header that the receiving endpoint (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 22-26) expects for authentication. The webhook endpoint checks req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] against CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, but refreshOAuthTokens never sends this header, meaning the sync request would fail authentication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — Secret verification fails open when CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset because a request with no matching header compares undefined equal to undefined.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 22-27, the secret verification compares `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret']` against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset (undefined), and a request comes in without that header (also undefined), the comparison `undefined !== undefined` is false, so the check passes. However, the earlier check at line 17-19 checks `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` which according to packages/lib/constants.ts requires both CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY to be set. So if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED would be falsy and the function would return 403 at line 18 before reaching the secret comparison. The finding appears to be a hallucination because the earlier guard prevents the scenario described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:73 — Updating a previously invalidated credential changes only its key and returns 200 while leaving invalid=true, so successful synchronization does not restore the integration.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, the code at lines 68-78 shows that when updating an existing credential, only the 'key' field is updated via prisma.credential.update(). The Credential model likely has an 'invalid' field (common pattern for OAuth credentials that have been revoked/expired). When syncing new valid credentials, if the credential was previously marked as invalid=true, this update would leave that flag unchanged, meaning the integration would still appear broken to the user despite having valid credentials. This is a real bug - the update should also set invalid=false to restore the integration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — The find-then-create sequence is non-atomic, allowing concurrent first-delivery webhooks to create duplicate credentials or fail one delivery after external state has advanced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a find-then-create pattern in app-credential.ts lines 57-87: first findFirst() is called to check if credential exists, then either update() or create() is called based on the result. This is indeed a race condition - if two concurrent webhook requests arrive for the same userId/appId combination, both could pass the findFirst check (finding no existing credential), and both would then attempt to create(), potentially resulting in duplicate credentials or a unique constraint violation. This is a real concurrency bug in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:56 — Decrypted credential JSON is never validated against the selected app's credential schema, so an authenticated malformed delivery is acknowledged and corrupts the live credential.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, the code decrypts the keys at line 53-55 using `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...))` but never validates that the decrypted JSON conforms to the expected credential schema for the specific app. The code then directly uses these keys in prisma.credential.update() or prisma.credential.create() without any schema validation. This means malformed but syntactically valid JSON could be stored as credentials, potentially corrupting the credential data. The finding correctly identifies that there's no validation against the app's credential schema after decryption.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The advertised access-token-and-expiry response contract does not actually accept or preserve an arbitrary expiry field because the computed Zod key becomes a literal property and unknown fields are stripped.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 5-10, the schema definition uses `[z.string().toString()]` as computed property keys. This doesn't create dynamic property matching - `z.string().toString()` returns '[object Object]' or similar string representation, not a dynamic key matcher. Zod doesn't support arbitrary key matching this way. The schema would create literal properties with those stringified values, not catch-all patterns. This means the schema won't properly validate responses with varying expiry field names (like 'expires_in', 'expiry_date', etc.) as the comments suggest it should. The code claims to 'Assume that any property with a number is the expiry' but the Zod schema doesn't actually implement this behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — With no configured webhook secret, an absent header compares as `undefined` and permits an unauthenticated credential write.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 22-27, the webhook secret check compares `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret']` against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured (undefined), and the request doesn't include the header (also undefined), then `undefined !== undefined` is false, meaning the check passes. However, looking more carefully at line 17-19, there's a prior check `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` which returns 403. APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is defined in constants.ts as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. So if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set, APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED would be falsy, and the endpoint would return 403 before reaching the secret comparison. This means the finding is incorrect - the code is protected by the earlier check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Credential-sync returns a Fetch `Response`, but it is treated as a `HubspotToken`, causing undefined token fields to be persisted.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the token refresh call with `refreshOAuthTokens()`. The `refreshOAuthTokens` function (in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns either a fetch Response object (when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true) or the result of refreshFunction(). When credential sync is enabled, it returns `response` which is a fetch Response, not the parsed token data. The original code expected `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken()` to return a HubspotToken directly. Now when credential sync is enabled, `hubspotRefreshToken` will be a Response object, and accessing `.accessToken`, `.refreshToken`, `.expiresIn` will be undefined, causing incorrect data to be persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The `any` callback and inferred union return erase whether callers receive a Fetch `Response` or an SDK-specific token object, allowing every adapter to assume an incompatible shape without type checking.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that refreshOAuthTokens in the diff (lines 3-21 of refreshOAuthTokens.ts) uses `refreshFunction: () => any` and returns either the result of refreshFunction() or a fetch Response, creating a union type that erases type safety. Looking at the diff, different callers pass different types: Google passes `fetchTokens.res`, HubSpot passes the result of `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken()`, and others pass fetch Response objects. The function returns these heterogeneous types without type checking. This is a legitimate architectural/type-safety concern introduced by the new code, though it's not a bug since the code may work at runtime - it's a design issue that could lead to future bugs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13 — Accepting `any` and `ZodTypeAny` and returning the whole safe-parse wrapper leaks validation mechanics while discarding the schema's inferred token type, which has already led callers to consume and persist the result inconsistently.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real design issue in the new parseRefreshTokenResponse function. Looking at the diff, the function accepts `any` for response and `z.ZodTypeAny` for schema (lines 12-13), and returns the SafeParseReturnType wrapper rather than the validated data. This is visible in how callers use it inconsistently - in GoogleCalendarService.ts line 96, the result is assigned directly to `key` without accessing `.data`, while in Office365CalendarService.ts line 261, it's used with `.success && tokenResponse.data`. The function also mutates the result by adding a default refresh_token (lines 24-26). This is a legitimate architectural concern about type safety and API design in newly added code, though it's not a bug since the code can still function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — Token validation is coupled to global environment state instead of the response source, so local refreshes that fall back because a credential has no userId are still parsed under the sync-endpoint contract.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 14-17, the function checks `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` to decide which schema to use. However, in refreshOAuthTokens.ts, when userId is null, it falls back to calling the local refreshFunction directly (line 16-17). The issue is that parseRefreshTokenResponse doesn't know whether the response came from the sync endpoint or the local refresh - it only checks global env vars. So if APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true but a credential has no userId (causing local refresh fallback), the response will still be parsed with minimumTokenResponseSchema instead of the proper app-specific schema, potentially causing validation issues or accepting malformed responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:40 — Resolving the app through both the database and `appStoreMetadata` creates two registries that must remain synchronized for the webhook to accept an integration.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the webhook handler at lines 37-48 first queries the database for the app by slug, then looks up appStoreMetadata using that same slug. If an app exists in the database but not in appStoreMetadata (or vice versa), the webhook will fail. This is a valid architectural concern about maintaining two sources of truth that must stay synchronized. The code shows: first `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug: reqBody.appSlug } })` at line 37, then `appStoreMetadata[app.slug as keyof typeof appStoreMetadata]` at line 46. This dual-lookup pattern could cause issues if the registries diverge, though it's a design concern rather than an immediate bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Every client construction unconditionally refreshes Salesforce tokens and writes the credential, adding a remote call and database write even while the access token is valid.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code unconditionally performs a token refresh (lines 72-88) every time the connection is constructed. Unlike other calendar services in this diff (like GoogleCalendarService, Office365CalendarService) which check token expiry before refreshing, the Salesforce implementation has no expiry check - it always calls the refresh endpoint and updates the database. This is a performance bug that adds unnecessary network calls and database writes on every operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync fetch has no abort timeout, so an unavailable sync service can indefinitely block expired-token booking requests.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts lines 6-14, the code performs a fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT without any timeout/abort controller. If the sync service is unavailable or slow, this fetch will hang indefinitely, blocking the token refresh operation and consequently any booking requests that require refreshed tokens. This is a real defect - network calls to external services should have timeouts to prevent indefinite blocking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — Sync mode returns a Fetch Response but this path reads a Gaxios `.data` field, so every Google token refresh through the sync endpoint falls back to the expired token.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, the code at line 86-96 shows that `refreshOAuthTokens` is called and returns `res`. When using the sync endpoint (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Fetch Response directly. However, the code then accesses `res?.data` on line 93 (`const token = res?.data`), which works for the Gaxios response from `myGoogleAuth.refreshToken()` but not for a Fetch Response. A Fetch Response doesn't have a `.data` property - you need to call `.json()` on it. This means when credential sync is enabled, `token` will be undefined, and the token refresh will fail silently, falling back to expired credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — Persisting the SafeParse result rather than its `.data` stores `{success,data}` as the Google credential and makes subsequent authentications fail validation.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, line 100 shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then line 101-103 shows `await prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })`. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function (shown in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns the result of `schema.safeParse(response)` which is an object with `{success, data, error}` structure, not the actual parsed data. The code should be using `key.data` instead of `key` when updating the credential. This would store the wrong structure and break subsequent authentication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Sync mode returns a Fetch Response where HubSpot expects a parsed token object, so refresh writes/uses undefined token fields and leaves the client unauthenticated.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the refreshOAuthTokens function wraps the original token creation call. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response object (from the sync endpoint). However, the code then uses hubspotRefreshToken directly as if it were a HubspotToken object with properties like accessToken and expiresIn. The fetch Response object doesn't have these properties, so the subsequent code would fail or use undefined values. This is a real bug where the return type mismatch causes incorrect behavior in sync mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 — The sync response is documented to omit refresh tokens, but the parser injects `"refresh_token"` and this merge overwrites the usable Office 365 refresh token.
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same underlying problem as the golden comment. Both describe that the parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly handles the refresh_token field - the golden comment says it sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when missing, and the candidate says the parser 'injects "refresh_token"' which overwrites the usable Office 365 refresh token. Both recognize this causes authentication/token refresh problems. The candidate correctly identifies the file location and the core issue of the refresh token being improperly handled during sync responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:93 — Saving the access-token-only sync response replaces the Teams credential and drops its refresh token, preventing recovery when the next token expires.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts, the refreshOAuthTokens function is called at line 60-78. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, refreshOAuthTokens returns the response from the sync endpoint (lines 6-14 in refreshOAuthTokens.ts), which only contains access_token and expiry. The responseBody is then used to update credentials. The minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts only requires access_token and a number (expiry), and if refresh_token is missing, it sets a dummy 'refresh_token' value. This means the original refresh_token from the credential would be lost when the credential is updated, breaking future token refreshes. This is a real bug in the credential sync flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — An unset CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET makes an absent header compare equal to undefined and bypasses webhook authentication

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at lines 23-26 of app-credential.ts, the code checks `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret'] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set (undefined), and the header is also not present in the request (undefined), then `undefined !== undefined` evaluates to `false`, meaning the check passes and authentication is bypassed. This is a real security vulnerability where an unset environment variable allows unauthenticated access to the webhook endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — No sync-enabled refresh test exercises a real Fetch Response, so the code reads the nonexistent res.data and silently keeps the expired token.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, the refreshOAuthTokens function wraps the original refresh call and returns either a custom fetch Response (when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) or the result of the refresh function. The original code did `const { res } = await myGoogleAuth.refreshToken(...)` and accessed `res?.data`. After the change, `res` is the direct return from refreshOAuthTokens. When credential sharing is enabled, this returns a fetch Response object which doesn't have a `.data` property - it would need `.json()` to parse. The code then does `const token = res?.data` which would be undefined for a fetch Response, causing `googleCredentials.access_token` and `expiry_date` to be set to undefined. This is a real bug in the credential sharing path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — No sync-enabled HubSpot test verifies the endpoint response is decoded before treating the Fetch Response itself as HubspotToken credentials.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the refreshOAuthTokens function wraps the original token refresh call. The original code directly assigned the result of hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken() to hubspotRefreshToken. With the new code, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response object (from lines 6-14 of refreshOAuthTokens.ts), not the decoded token data. The HubSpot code then tries to use this Response object as HubspotToken credentials without calling .json() on it first. This is a real bug - the Response object would be used directly instead of the parsed JSON token data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — The shared provider-routing helper has no tests for enabled, disabled, team-owned, non-2xx, or malformed-response branches despite changing refresh behavior across six integrations.
